group.passage:
Svalbard is one of the northernmost inhabited places on Earth. It is located in the Arctic Ocean, halfway between Norway and the North Pole, sitting between longitude 10° and 35° East and latitude 74° and 81° North. It is approximately 400 miles away (650km) from the North Pole and 580 miles (930km) from mainland Norway. The Svalbard islands are dominated by glaciers, snowfields, and icy fjords, with little vegetation and a harsh climate. Despite this, the coastal areas are warmer than expected, thanks to the Gulf Stream. Its remote location and extreme conditions give Svalbard a unique, otherworldly atmosphere.
Svalbard’s history began in the 16th century when European explorers, including Dutchman Willem Barentsz, first sighted the islands. Initially, the archipelago was used for whaling, and later it became a key location for Arctic exploration. Permanent settlements first appeared in the early 1900s, driven by coal mining, which shaped the region’s economy for much of the 20th century. Today, remnants of the mining industry remain, especially in towns like Longyearbyen, the largest settlement.
One of the most enthralling legends of Svalbard is that it is “illegal to die.” Unlike other major places, this area has a precise temperature and environment that causes permafrost, permanently frozen ground. Because of this, corpses can’t decompose within the area, meaning they need to be shipped back to the mainland to be buried, which is why Svalbard has rules about this.
Governed by Norway, Svalbard has a unique political status. Under the Svalbard Treaty of 1920, citizens of all countries can live and work there without visas, making it a truly international community. The local government manages affairs with a focus on sustainable development and environmental preservation.
Svalbard’s economy has shifted from coal mining to a focus on scientific research and tourism. It serves as a hub for international research, particularly in the fields of climate change and Arctic ecosystems. Meanwhile, tourism is thriving. For tourists, the summer months are ideal for outdoor activities like glacier hikes and wildlife watching, while the winter polar nights provide the chance to see the Northern Lights in a breathtaking Arctic setting. Whether for adventure or scientific discovery, Svalbard offers an unforgettable experience at the edge of the world.

figures.label: the map（第2題）
figures.caption: 以北極為中心的北極地區地圖，圖上標有 (A)(B)(C)(D) 四個字母
figures.description: 黑白極地投影地圖，置於第2題題幹與選項之間：中心為北極點，標示「The North Pole」與「+ 90° N」；陸地為灰色、海洋為白色。圖上畫有 80° N 與 70° N 兩圈緯線（標示在北極點右下方），以及一圈虛線標示的「The Arctic Circle」（北極圈，標示在地圖下方）；多條經線由北極點向外放射，左上角標有「30° W」「20° W」兩條經線，另有一條經線沿線標示「The Prime Meridian」（本初子午線），由地圖左上方斜向通往北極點。以本初子午線為界，20° W、30° W 所在的一側（往地圖上方、格陵蘭方向）為西經，另一側（往地圖左下方、斯堪地那維亞半島與俄羅斯北岸方向）為東經。四個字母的位置：(A) 標在地圖上方的大島格陵蘭內陸，位於 30° W 經線再往西（約西經 40 度、北緯 75 度，西半球）；(B) 標在緊鄰本初子午線東側的一組群島旁（約東經 15–25 度、北緯 78–80 度），位置在北極點與左側斯堪地那維亞半島（挪威）之間；(C) 標在 (B) 以東、緯度較低、靠近歐亞大陸（俄羅斯）北岸的一座狹長大島上（約東經 60 度、北緯 75 度）；(D) 標在更東邊、俄羅斯（西伯利亞）北方、北極點正下方的一組島嶼旁（約東經 90–105 度、北緯 80–81 度）。其餘陸地為環繞北極海的歐、亞、北美各洲北部。
